citation: Dominik Blain, Maxime Noiseux (Cobalt AI). 'Broken by Default: A Formal Verification Study of Security Vulnerabilities in AI-Generated Code'. arXiv:2604.05292 (cs.CR; cross-list cs.AI, cs.SE), v1 7 Apr 2026, v2 8 Apr 2026. https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05292
source_tier: Preprint (arXiv, not peer reviewed; 8 pages, 6 tables). Authors' own tool evaluated.
access_status: Abstract page and arXiv HTML v2 read via a summarising fetch tool; the PDF body could not be decoded directly. Quotes and table figures are therefore second-hand through the summariser. [uncertain]
sponsor_and_incentive: Authors are the founder and co-founder of Cobalt AI, which makes COBALT, the Z3-based tool the paper evaluates and promotes. No funding or conflict-of-interest statement found in the paper. This is a self-evaluation by a vendor.
exact_quotes: Abstract: 'Across all models, 55.8% of artifacts contain at least one COBALT-identified vulnerability' (abstract). Corpus: '3,500 code artifacts (500 prompts x 7 models)' (s3.2). Prompts 'designed to be representative of real developer tasks, not adversarial jailbreaks' (s3.1). Results 'should not be extrapolated to all possible LLM usage patterns' (s1.2). 'no model achieves grade C or better' (results). Verbatim wording relayed via summariser. [uncertain]
date_and_recency: Submitted 7 April 2026, revised 8 April 2026. Models queried via production APIs at temperature 0, results 'as of April 2026'.
key_claims: Across 3,500 LLM-generated artifacts for security-critical prompts, 55.8% contain at least one COBALT finding; 1,055 are formally proven with Z3 satisfiable witnesses (concrete exploit inputs). Explicit security instructions cut the rate only about 4 points. Six existing tools together miss 97.8% of Z3-proven findings. Models flag their own vulnerable code 78.7% of the time when asked to review it, yet generate it 55.8% of the time by default.
headline_figures: Unit: one generated artifact per prompt per model; vulnerable = at least one COBALT finding. Overall 55.8% (mean). Per model: GPT-4o 62.4% (F), Llama 4 Scout 60.6% (F), Llama 3.3 70B 58.4% (D), Mistral Large 57.8% (D), GPT-4.1 54.0% (D), Claude Haiku 4.5 49.2% (D), Gemini 2.5 Flash 48.4% (D). 1,055 artifacts are Z3 SAT (formally proven), a subset of the 55.8%; the rest are PATTERN MATCH findings with Z3 encoding pending. Security prompt: 64.8% to 60.8% on the 50-prompt v1 corpus (250 artifacts). Tool comparison: 88 of 90 Z3 SAT findings missed by all tools (97.8%). Self-review: 70/89 = 78.7%. ASan: 6 of 7 selected findings confirmed runtime faults. Table figures second-hand. [uncertain]
sample_unit_and_population: 500 prompt templates, 100 each across five CWE areas (MEM CWE-131/190, INT CWE-190/195, AUTH CWE-916, CRYPTO CWE-327/330, INP CWE-89/22/78), 7 LLMs, 3,500 artifacts. Mostly C/C++ for memory/integer, Python for the others. Single-shot prompts, not real repositories. Ablation, tool and self-review experiments use only the 50-prompt v1 subset (250 artifacts).
observed_vs_stated: Observed: generated code analysed by a tool, with some runtime confirmation. Not developer behaviour or self-report. Self-review experiment is model output, not human belief.
what_makes_trust_justified: The paper argues pattern-based scanners and security-prompting are insufficient, and that formal verification (SMT solving, exploit witnesses) of generated code is needed. Authors promote their own tool.
what_it_costs: Not quantified in the material read. [uncertain]
failure_mode_class: Security: memory safety, integer, weak hashing/crypto, injection vulnerabilities in generated code.
control_that_would_have_prevented: Not an incident study. The paper's implied control is solver-backed verification before merge; reviewing by the same model caught 78.7% of its own flawed code.
limitations_stated: Five CWE categories only; temperature 0 only; no multi-turn or RAG; ablations only on the 50-prompt subset; not to be extrapolated to all LLM usage; Go, Rust, JavaScript left to future work.
counter_evidence: Vendor self-evaluation, unreviewed. The 55.8% counts any COBALT finding including unproven pattern matches; only 1,055 of 3,500 (about 30%) are Z3-proven. The abstract's 'six tools' figure mixes subsets: 7.6% is Semgrep+Bandit only on 250 artifacts, and CodeQL ran only on the 90 Z3 SAT artifacts. Generation rate and review detection rate measure different things. Claude rows in ablation and self-review use Claude 3.5 Sonnet, not Haiku 4.5. Prompts are short single-function tasks, so real-world rates may differ. No human or false-positive baseline seen. [uncertain]
verification_status: Core figures (55.8%, per-model rates, unit) read in arXiv HTML via a summariser tool and match the abstract page and search snippet. Not checked against the raw PDF text or the dataset repo (github.com/dom-omg/bbd-dataset). Treat as checked-but-secondhand. [uncertain]
usable_claim: A vendor preprint (April 2026) that formally analysed 3,500 single-prompt code artifacts from seven LLMs found at least one flagged vulnerability in 55.8%, with about 1,055 backed by solver-generated exploit witnesses; adding a security instruction lowered the rate by roughly 4 points.
do_not_use: The 97.8% 'tools miss' figure as a general claim (it is 88 of 90 on a small subset). 55.8% as 'formally proven' or as a real-world production rate. Any ranking of models as safety verdicts. The 78.7% vs 55.8% comparison as like for like.
overlap_with_existing_essays: Not checked against the Verification Gap or Checking Isn't Catching essays in this task. [uncertain]
